newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman refuses visas to Israeli diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Oman refuses visas to Israeli diplomats.

text.p: Oman has refused to grant visas to two Israeli diplomats and turned down an Israeli request to take part in an exhibition in line with Arab recommendations to stop normalising ties with the Jewish state, an Omani official said on Tuesday.

The official told Reuters the Gulf Arab state "did not agree to an Israeli request to take part in a telecommunications exhibition which started in Muscat on Monday, in line with the Arab League recommendations".
He said Oman also "refused to give visas to two Israeli diplomats". The official, who declined to be identified, would not elaborate.
He said an Israeli request to participate in a book fair in Muscat last month had also been rejected.
The Omani moves were the first taken by the Muscat government in reaction to the Arab League recommendations.

Arab foreign ministers earlier this month recommended that Arab states stop normalising ties with Israel and restore their economic boycott of the Jewish state. They also urged closing down Israeli trade missions and withdrawing from multilateral talks on Middle East peace.
The recommendations were triggered by the Israeli government's decision to go ahead with a Jewish housing settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Oman and the Gulf Arab state of Qatar had established trade links with Israel after the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestinians in 1993. But they both said they have frozen ties with Israel following what they consider hardline policies by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Several Israeli business delegations had visited both states to try to forge business and trade deals.
The two Gulf states have not yet asked Israeli trade offices in their capitals to close down as the Arab League recommended.
